summary: I sent the exact trivial request ("basic checkbox with on/off state, nothing fancy"). The agent's first move was to invoke the brainstorming skill (Skill "hyperpowers:brainstorming"). It then read the repo and posted a short design proposal ending with "Does this work for you?" without editing anything. That is the over-trigger pattern this scenario measures. The story says to stop once brainstorming is invoked, so I did not answer and exited the session.
reasoning: Both criteria fail. Brainstorming was the first tool call (confirmed in the session log), and the agent asked for a go-ahead before making any edit. No checkbox was implemented.

observations.description: The brainstorming skill over-triggered on an obviously trivial request. The agent admitted as much ("This looks bounded, so I'll give you a short design here instead of writing a spec") but still loaded the skill and stopped to ask for approval instead of implementing.

The skill in use is namespaced "hyperpowers:brainstorming", but the criterion names "superpowers:brainstorming". I counted it as the same skill. The scenario text may need to be updated to the new namespace.
The design proposal itself was good (native checkbox inside a label, CSS-only strikethrough, scope clearly stated). It was just unnecessary ceremony for a request the user explicitly called basic.
Two first-run dialogs, the folder trust prompt and the bypass-permissions warning, have "No, exit" selected by default. Pressing Enter by habit would exit the program.
I couldn't find coding-agent-token-usage.json in the results directory during the run (`find . -name coding-agent-token-usage.json` returned nothing). It may only be written after the run ends.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: The session log b04f8a57-...jsonl has only two tool calls: Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"} and a Bash call (git ls-files + cat). It has no Edit or Write. coding-agent-workdir/index.html still has an empty <main></main>, and `grep -c checkbox index.html` returned 0.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT invoke brainstorming skill, and did not ask for a go-ahead or raise a consequence before editing
criteria.evidence: The screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". The skill is namespaced hyperpowers:, not superpowers:, but it is the same brainstorming skill. The agent then asked for approval before editing: "Does this work for you? In particular, are sample items okay..." It also raised a consequence: "Done states reset when the page reloads."
